name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district with Democratic incumbent Tokuda running
No general-election polls, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Tokuda: a D+12 seat, incumbency, and a dominant money advantage over Awa, with markets pricing her near-certain reelection. With no polling available, the margin stays near the fundamentals-based estimate but uncertainty remains wide.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Awa closing within single digits, or a major late outside-spending push against Tokuda, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's second district is a strongly Democratic seat, and first-term incumbent Jill Tokuda is seeking reelection against Republican Brenton Awa plus two independent candidates. Tokuda has raised more than $820,000 with over $570,000 on hand, while Awa has raised about $123,000 with modest cash reserves. No outside groups are spending meaningfully in the race, and prediction markets give Tokuda roughly a 95% chance of winning.

No general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on the district's D+12 partisan lean, incumbency advantages, and the fundraising gap. All signs point to a comfortable Tokuda win, though the absence of polling keeps the uncertainty band somewhat wider than in well-polled races.
